title: Mixed-integer nonlinear optimization
contribution: Six-author survey that organizes MINLP methods around relaxation and constraint enforcement on two axes (convex/nonconvex, single-/multitree), derives the convex-MINLP methods from outer approximation, states the corrected OA theory and worst case, argues for reformulation with solver numbers, and adds nonconvex relaxations, heuristics, mixed-integer optimal control and a software map (read as Argonne preprint ANL/MCS-P3060-1121, Nov 2012).
problem_entry: MINLP as the most general paradigm containing NLP and MILP, NP-hard and in the nonconvex integer case undecidable, so the scope is restricted to the decidable case (X compact or convex functions) and to deterministic methods (pp. 5, 11-13).
key_idea: Every MINLP algorithm combines a relaxation (integrality, supporting hyperplanes, convex underestimators) with constraint enforcement (cuts or branching); convex methods are derived from one another (Benders from OA by multiplier aggregation, ECP as OA without NLP solves, LP/NLP-BB as branch-and-cut on the OA MILP) and hybrids are judged the most efficient (pp. 4, 7-11, 31-39).
assumptions: Assumption 3.1: X bounded polyhedral, f and c C^2 and convex, a CQ on the convex hull of the feasible set (called 'technical', p. 22); NLP nodes solved to global optimality (p. 24); finite integer set for OA (p. 34); factorable functions with known expressions for nonconvex MINLP (p. 64); Lipschitz/boundedness conditions and integer-independent path constraints for MIOCP (pp. 88, 91-94).
proof_devices: NLP-BB finiteness by reduction to MILP B&B once nodes are solved globally (Prop. 3.1, p. 24)
OA finiteness via cutoff eta <= U - eps excluding revisited integer assignments, convexity giving supporting hyperplanes; feasibility problem and Lemma 3.1 for infeasible subproblems (pp. 31-34)
corrected OA equivalence: converse fails, Bonami et al. 2008 counterexample, proof credited jointly (Thm 3.1, p. 32)
Hijazi et al. worst case: distance sqrt(n)/2 > (n-1)/4, one vertex per cut, transferred to Benders and ECP as relaxations of OA (p. 34)
Benders cut derived from OA cuts via multiplier aggregation, complementary slackness and stationarity (pp. 34-35)
LP/NLP-BB convergence as corollary of OA (Thm 3.3, pp. 37-38)
disaggregation: projection argument for tighter OA, then two linearization points defeat the worst case (pp. 43-44)
sBB convergence via finite consistency (Thm 5.1, p. 70)
FBBT non-termination counterexample x1 = alpha x2, x2 = alpha x1 (p. 74)
factorable relaxation vs convex hull on x1^2 + x2^2 >= 1 (pp. 75-76)
MIOCP state-deviation and sum-up-rounding bounds, cited from Sager et al. 2012 (pp. 91-92)
binary QP convexification by eigenvalue shift (p. 14)
experiments: Illustrative only: Syn20M04M tree sizes and times (MINOTAUR 264,000 nodes unsolved in 2 h, BONMIN-BB and MINLPBB about 150,000, hybrid OA 9 s, MINOTAUR with presolve 2.3 s, pp. 39-42); performance profile on Syn*/Rsyn* (presolve solves 20% more instances, p. 42; machine, time limit and versions not stated); facility location n=m=40, 53,000 s vs 2 s (p. 43); rocket-car MIOCP in MUSCOD-II, weak bound about 37 vs exact 64 (pp. 90-92).
positioning: Situates itself among Grossmann, Grossmann-Kravanja, Bonami et al., Floudas and the Lee-Leyffer IMA volume, excludes MILP/NLP subproblems and three neighbouring topics (pp. 12-13); credits OA to Duran-Grossmann, adopts the Bonami et al. correction and the Hijazi worst case (pp. 31-34); recasts generalized Benders as a weaker derivative of OA (pp. 34-35); defers to Tawarmalani-Sahinidis and Burer-Letchford for nonconvex MINLP (p. 57); cites own solvers and libraries throughout (pp. 16, 39-42, 96, 99).
writing: Organizing concept on p. 7, a tiny computed example with a figure for each technique (pp. 7, 40-41, 48-49, 54, 64-65, 76, 84), pseudocode boxes, theorems quoted with provenance (p. 53), moderate hedging (pp. 14, 99), first-person plural for own experience (p. 39); preprint slips (pp. 6, 38, 44) and no conclusion section (ends with software, pp. 94-100).
limits_future: Gaps stated locally: split disjunctions unused in MINLP (p. 27), l1-penalty pseudocost update suggested (pp. 26-27), NLP warm starts unsuccessful (p. 27), disjunctive-cut separation hard and little tested (p. 50), piecewise-linear limited to few arguments (p. 64), RLT/SDP hierarchies too large (p. 79), gamma(n_omega) conjectured O(log n_omega) (p. 92), integer-dependent constraints in MIOCP not covered (p. 94).

method_links.note: Modelling practices: evaluation failures as cause of solver failure and bounded-auxiliary repair, convex over nonconvex and linear over nonlinear, lower degree of nonlinearity for NLP convergence, coefficient tightening and disaggregation turning hours into seconds.

OA worst case, corrected OA equivalence with counterexample, FBBT non-termination, factorable relaxation vs hull, max-fractional branching no better than random; the worst case is followed by a remedy (disaggregation).

Building blocks relaxation and constraint enforcement; Leyffer (2001) implicit bounds and QP-diving exploiting QP warm starts; FilMINT as LP/NLP-BB inside a MILP solver; MINOTAUR modifies computational graphs.
Batch model on MacMINLP, IBM/CMU Syn*/Rsyn* instances, MacMINLP and minlp.org libraries, NEOS, Sager's MIOCP benchmark library.

Rule of thumb by class (hybrids most efficient) and an own-solver loss reported (MINOTAUR vs hybrid OA), but the performance profile states no fairness rule, machine, time limit or versions and compares the authors' solver with and without presolve.

NLP machinery carried into the tree (l1 exact-penalty pseudocosts, NLP feasibility problem as infeasibility certificate); MIOCP named as a class with a library. The carried-in CQ is labelled 'technical' and assumed on the whole convex hull (the Method 2 limitation).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: minimal-requirement reading of a convergence proof
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: States that NLP-BB convergence needs only global optimality at pruned nodes and that non-leaf nodes need only a branching variable, then uses that freedom for inexact SQP solves, implicit bounds and QP-diving.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: one tiny computed example and figure per technique
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Objective-variable trick, coefficient tightening, a numerically computed disjunctive cut, MISOCP Gomory cut, DAG of a small MINLP, convex-hull gap, Undercover graph.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: method family as relaxations of one master method
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Benders cuts derived from OA cuts and called weaker, ECP as OA without NLP solves, so the OA worst case transfers to both.

transferable: Move the argument of a function undefined outside a domain into a new bounded variable (x2 = sin(x1), x2 >= 0) so bound-respecting NLP solvers never evaluate it there (p. 15).
For big-M on/off constraints whose binary also switches the variable bounds, tighten M by evaluating c(0) instead of solving a nonconvex maximization (pp. 41-42).
Disaggregate h(g(x)) and sum_j h_j(a_j^T x) into auxiliary variables before OA-based algorithms and check on the Hijazi worst case that two linearization points suffice (pp. 43-44).
Write down what the convergence proof needs and spend the slack on inexact or surrogate solves at non-leaf nodes (pp. 24, 29).
Derive weaker variants from the strongest method (Benders from OA by multiplier aggregation) and state the strength order (pp. 34-35).
Test a generic relaxation scheme against the known convex hull of a two-variable set (pp. 75-76).
Show one hard instance with tree sizes and times for own solver, competitors and reformulated model, then a performance profile over the family, adding machine, time limit and versions (pp. 40-42).
coauthors: Pietro Belotti, Christian Kirches, Jeff Linderoth, James Luedtke, Ashutosh Mahajan

quotes.text: In many practical instances, the MINLP solvers fail, because the nonlinear solver generates an iterate at which the nonlinear functions cannot be evaluated.
In fact, at any non-leaf node of the tree, we need only to provide a branching variable.
